blocks.text: Objects and classes lie at the heart of this book, and, since the introduction of PHP 5 over a decade ago, they have lain at the heart of PHP, too. In this chapter, I establish the groundwork for more in-depth coverage of objects and design by examining PHP’s core object-oriented features. If you are new to object-oriented programming, you should read this chapter carefully. This chapter will cover the following topics:

items: Classes and objects: Declaring classes and instantiating objects
Constructor methods: Automating the setup of your objects
Primitive and class types: Why type matters
Inheritance: Why we need inheritance and how to use it
Visibility: Streamlining your object interfaces and protecting your methods and properties from meddling

payload.markdown: The first barrier to understanding object-oriented programming is the strange and wonderful relationship between the class and the object. For many people, it is this relationship that represents the first moment of revelation, the first flash of object-oriented excitement. So let’s not skimp on the fundamentals.

blocks.text: The first barrier to understanding object-oriented programming is the strange and wonderful relationship between the class and the object. For many people, it is this relationship that represents the first moment of revelation, the first flash of object-oriented excitement. So let’s not skimp on the fundamentals.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Constructor: __construct initialises each new object; promoted parameters collapse the boilerplate.
Inheritance: Deriving a class from a base class to reuse and specialise its behaviour.
Interfaces: A pure contract of method signatures with no implementation.
Properties & Methods: Class state held in properties, and behaviour implemented as methods.
Visibility & Encapsulation: public, protected and private control who may read or write a member.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Chapter 1 core idea: The central idea of chapter 1 in one plain sentence.
